assessments.reasoning: All seven contiguous parts of the SPDX repository’s pinned json/details/LGPL-2.1-only.json cover 101,590 bytes, SHA-256 c26841db6b15d7b020d9e74412ce104e5cff445ebcb27b4c2ee91bf8ebb1d593. Part 1 reports isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Part 4 gives licenseId=LGPL-2.1-only, explains the election, and supplies the only header. Its seeAlso cites GNU’s standalone and regular old-license HTML pages and OSI’s LGPL-2.1-only page. These are alternative references, not independent inspections.

The GitHub API for spdx/license-list-data identifies annotated tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b as v3.29.0. Its target type is commit and its target SHA is 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, exactly the revision in the claim and the detail URL. GitHub reports the tag as unsigned. The evidence establishes the repository’s release mapping.

The complete GNU archive text matches the scoped publisher digest. Section 0 identifies whose notice applies the license, and §13 describes the effect of specifying a numbered version with “any later version.” The application example uses that broader election. These passages establish the edition and explain why an only grant requires its own applicable notice. SPDX supplies the identifier.

challenge.method: Compared the only record’s full license text, §13, standard header, and comments with the FSF application example and the sibling LGPL-2.1-or-later record. Tested whether the common heading or application example alone selects the only identifier.
challenge.results: Both records carry the February 1999 heading and reproduce the later-version sample. Only the only record’s variant-specific header stops at version 2.1. The word “alone” in the claim describes that election. The example header does not require the literal word “only.” A recipient choosing to follow 2.1 under a broader grant still received the later-version option.

limitations: “SPDX 3.29.0” here means release 3.29.0 of the SPDX License List. Its matching template and header guide identification. The applicable copyright holder’s or authorized party’s notice establishes the grant, version choice, and any modifications for the code in question.

Both correspondence records use the same subject, edition, and publisher digest and have empty conditions arrays. Their statements distinguish the elections. A lookup that ignores the notice and treats both keys as unconditional aliases would lose that distinction.
reasoning: SPDX License List 3.29.0 records LGPL-2.1-only for code whose applicable notice specifies LGPL version 2.1 alone. The identifier, name, comments, and standard header agree. The apparent wording inconsistency is real but has a specific explanation: the same record’s licenseText reproduces the publisher’s sample notice offering later versions, while its standardLicenseHeader ends the election at “version 2.1.” The proposed correspondence holds for the notice described in the claim. It would be incorrect to describe the pinned FSF sample itself as version-2.1-only.
